where: section 2 body text and quiz Q1, Q4
problem: The integral limits are written inline as plain letters, e.g. "∫ab f(x,y) dx" and "∫cd (∫ab f(x,y) dx) dy". On a phone a student can read "∫ab" as the integral of the product a·b, and "∫cd" as ∫(cd). The tags <sub> and <sup> are available and the rest of the chapter already uses them (∫<sub>a</sub><sup>b</sup>).
fix: Write every limit with sub/sup tags: ∫<sub>a</sub><sup>b</sup> f(x,y) dx, ∫<sub>c</sub><sup>d</sup> (∫<sub>a</sub><sup>b</sup> f(x,y) dx) dy, and similarly in the Q1 and Q4 answers.

problem: The figure states a final value of 4 for "the double integral" over R = [0,2]×[0,1] but never says which function is being integrated. A number without an integrand is meaningless, and a student may think the integral of any function over that rectangle is 4.
fix: Name the integrand in the caption and the aria text, e.g. "f(x,y) = x + 2y on R = [0,2]×[0,1]; inner in x, outer in y, final value 4".

problem: "signed area of the slice of the surface z = f(x,y) along the line at that fixed y" calls the quantity a slice area. The slice of the surface is a curve; the integral is the area between that curve and the x-axis in the plane y = constant. As written, a student may think the inner integral gives the arc length or the area of the curve itself.
fix: Say: it is the signed area, in the plane y = constant, between the curve z = f(x,y) and the x-axis, from x = a to x = b.
